react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis — converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway with extreme statistical significance (RaMP FDR 1.5e-14; MetaboAnalystR p = 1.03e-06; mummichog p = 0.0018, overlap 12/13). Six tryptophan-adjacent metabolites are differentially abundant: the precursor L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), the decarboxylation product tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), the serotonin-pathway intermediates serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598), and the kynurenine-branch metabolites 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722). The simultaneous elevation of both the serotonin/melatonin arm and the kynurenine/NAD+ arm (via WP:WP4210 tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR 1.1e-10) indicates global tryptophan catabolism remodeling rather than blockade of a single branch. The kynurenine-pathway drivers quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid are neuroactive intermediates; their dysregulation carries implications for neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The Reactome module Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.5e-08) confirms the serotonergic arm independently. Putrescine (KEGG:C00134) and 3-sulfinoalanine (KEGG:C00606) additionally suggest polyamine and cysteine metabolism co-disruption, consistent with the broad amino-acid metabolism signal captured by REACT:R-HSA-71291 (Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives, FDR 3.2e-13). L-Leucine (KEGG:C00123) appears as a peripheral hit in valine/leucine/isoleucine degradation and amino acid metabolism. The InChIKey conflict between L-tryptophan and serotonin (shared first-block QIVBCDIJIAJPQS) reflects their structural kinship as indole-ethylamine derivatives and is not a data artefact. The cross-paradigm consensus firmly establishes tryptophan metabolism as the central biological story.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is overwhelmingly defined by disruption of tryptophan metabolism. Across two independent over-representation analyses — RaMP-DB (drawing on KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome and SMPDB) and MetaboAnalystR (KEGG-specific) — the pathway 'Tryptophan metabolism' (KEGG:hsa00380 / KEGG:map00380) is the unanimous top hit with a combined FDR of 1.50 × 10⁻¹⁴ and a raw p-value of 1.03 × 10⁻⁶, representing a 667-fold enrichment in the RaMP result. Five metabolites from the input list — L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid — were mapped by both tools into this pathway, with quinolinic acid captured additionally by RaMP. Within the RaMP WikiPathways tier, the same biochemical signal appears as 'Tryptophan metabolism' (WP:WP465, rank 3, FDR = 1.26 × 10⁻¹¹, 5 hits, 484-fold enrichment) and as the kynurenine-route sub-pathway 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (WP:WP4210, rank 5, FDR = 1.10 × 10⁻¹⁰, 4 hits). The serotonergic branch is further corroborated by 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (REACT:R-HSA-209931, rank 9, FDR = 3.47 × 10⁻⁸, 3 hits). L-Leucine (KEGG:C00123) appeared only in the broader Reactome 'Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives' (REACT:R-HSA-71291) and in peripheral KEGG hits with nominal p-values ≥ 0.044, indicating it is a secondary, non-specific signal. The driver metabolites are therefore the five tryptophan-pathway intermediates — L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and quinolinic acid — whose coordinated differential abundance implicates the central tryptophan metabolic axis as the biological storyline.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is dominated by tryptophan-derived molecules, producing one of the strongest cross-paradigm enrichment signals observed. Across three independent analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network activity scoring — the pathway "Tryptophan metabolism" emerged as the unambiguous top hit, with FDR or p-values many orders of magnitude below significance thresholds. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the pathway entry point; it is metabolised via the biogenic amine branch to produce serotonin (C00780) and subsequently melatonin (C01598), while the alternative kynurenine branch generates quinolinic acid (C03722) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). Tryptamine (C00398) represents a decarboxylation shunt off the main route. L-Leucine (C00123) and putrescine (C00134) appear in broad amino-acid metabolism catalogues reported by RaMP ORA but do not achieve pathway-specific significance in KEGG-only methods; their enrichment is consistent with the metabolic milieu of a tryptophan-perturbation experiment rather than a dedicated branch-point signal. Putrescine additionally appears in the mummichog urea-cycle/amino-group sub-pathway. The convergent evidence across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms supports a primary perturbation of tryptophan catabolism, most consistent with activation of the kynurenine–NAD+ arm, alterations in serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis, and peripheral biogenic amine turnover.

{
  "narrative_text": "Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis — converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway with extreme statistical significance (RaMP FDR 1.5e-14; MetaboAnalystR p = 1.03e-06; mummichog p = 0.0018, overlap 12/13). Six tryptophan-adjacent metabolites are differentially abundant: the precursor L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), the decarboxylation product tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), the serotonin-pathway intermediates serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598), and the kynurenine-branch metabolites 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722). The simultaneous elevation of both the serotonin/melatonin arm and the kynurenine/NAD+ arm (via WP:WP4210 tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR 1.1e-10) indicates global tryptophan catabolism remodeling rather than blockade of a single branch. The kynurenine-pathway drivers quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid are neuroactive intermediates; their dysregulation carries implications for neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The InChIKey conflict between L-tryptophan and serotonin (shared first-block QIVBCDIJIAJPQS) reflects their structural kinship as indole-ethylamine derivatives and is not a data artefact. Six tryptophan-adjacent metabolites are differentially abundant: the precursor L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), the decarboxylation product tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), the serotonin-pathway intermediates serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598), and the kynurenine-branch metabolites 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) and quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722). The simultaneous elevation of both the serotonin/melatonin arm and the kynurenine/NAD+ arm (via WP:WP4210 tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR 1.1e-10) indicates global tryptophan catabolism remodeling rather than blockade of a single branch. The kynurenine-pathway drivers quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid are neuroactive intermediates; their dysregulation carries implications for neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The Reactome module Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.5e-08) confirms the serotonergic arm independently. Putrescine (KEGG:C00134) and 3-sulfinoalanine (KEGG:C00606) additionally suggest polyamine and cysteine metabolism co-disruption, consistent with the broad amino-acid metabolism signal captured by REACT:R-HSA-71291 (Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives, FDR 3.2e-13). L-Leucine (KEGG:C00123) appears as a peripheral hit in valine/leucine/isoleucine degradation and amino acid metabolism. The InChIKey conflict between L-tryptophan and serotonin (shared first-block QIVBCDIJIAJPQS) reflects their structural kinship as indole-ethylamine derivatives and is not a data artefact.
